neighbours.label: physical quantities and their units in science text (power, pressure, volt, pascal, becquerel)
fire: In physics class we learned that power is the rate at which work is done.
Water pressure is the force that pushes water through the pipes in a house.
The battery supplies nine volts to the small motor in the toy.
Engineers measured a stress of two hundred pascals on the beam.
Readings near the reactor showed 500 becquerels per cubic metre of air.
The transformer steps the voltage down from 240 volts to 12 volts.
Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 101 kilopascals.
Electrical power in watts equals voltage multiplied by current.
quiet: In history class we learned that the empire fell after a long war.
Water is the drink that most people choose with dinner at home.
The battery is hidden under a small cover in the toy.
Engineers painted the beam a bright shade of blue last week.
Readings near the lake showed many birds nesting in the reeds.
The transformer sits in a grey box at the end of our street.
Life at sea level is easier for people who dislike the mountains.
Electrical work in old houses should be done by a licensed person.
